answer: ember binding ties each agent's reputation to a continuously updated local model whose weights are co-trained with its own historical predictions, so a fresh sybil can never inherit prior standing; copper fees therefore scale with the cumulative log-likelihood gap between the clone and the genuine trajectory, making thousands of identities cost more than linear retraining; plume verification still fails when an attacker steals the original checkpoint, since all seeded copies then share the same authentic gradient history.
